starting_question: Does a peptidase-like fold itself hydrolyze cell wall or activate another enzyme?
actual_observations: E1: Authors: the fold resembles active LytM but lacks its Zn-coordinating residues; no catalytic Zn is present.
E2: Authors: stable, septally localized variants fail normal cell separation and show impaired AmiB activation (Table 1).
E3: Authors: direct complex detection failed; a proposed regulatory-helix interaction remained a model.
E4: Root: parsed 20 Table 1 rows and selected 5 stable/localized/function-defective variants; mapped deposited residues and ligand records independently.
annotation_consequence: Supports amidase activation rather than copying metallopeptidase catalysis. Exact binding mechanism remains unestablished by this 2013 study.
verification_scope: 2013 complete relevant Results/Discussion/Methods and Table1 read via primary BioC; 2010 primary abstract/targeted indexed results only. Actual PDBe molecule/contact/residue checks and Table1 parsing saved. No new structural alignment or binding assay.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published results known. Authors performed all experiments; our retrieval, table selection and comparison choices are identified in traces. No blind discovery.
experiment_dependence: Authors performed the biological experiments; no cultures, mutants, enzymology or microscopy repeated here.

organism: Thermotoga maritima; separate Escherichia coli comparison
starting_question: Is TsaE needed for chemical transfer, product release, or restoring repeated catalytic operation?
actual_observations: T1: Authors 2018: TmTsaBD makes one product per complex without TsaE; product tRNA dissociates. ATPase-deficient TsaE does not sustain turnover.
T2: Authors 2019: switch variants retain robust ATPase yet lose efficient repeated t6A synthesis, separating hydrolysis from functional coupling.
T3: Authors 2015: E.coli W109A retains endpoint t6A formation despite low ATPase. Assays and organisms differ; the 2018 paper explicitly leaves reconciliation open.
annotation_consequence: Supports an ATP-hydrolysis-dependent reset contribution in the tested Thermotoga system. Do not equate ATPase capacity with successful coupling or silently generalize across species.
verification_scope: 2018 complete relevant single/multiple-turnover Results/Methods and Discussion; 2019 relevant full Results/Methods/Discussion; 2015 relevant binding/mutant Results, Discussion and full supplementary assay section inspected. No new time-course measurements or kinetic fits.

starting_question: Does a stress-associated LytM protein cleave peptidoglycan or alter amidase action?
actual_observations: Authors: ActS alone lacks detected PG cleavage; adding it activates amidases in vitro.
Authors: overexpression rescues activator-deficient separation but not triple-amidase loss; in-vivo preference is narrower than the in-vitro panel.
Authors: actS deletion suppresses lysis of an LPS-transport/ldtF perturbation; direct LdtF control remains unproven.
annotation_consequence: Amidase activator with conditional envelope effects. Neither growth rescue nor stress association establishes direct hydrolase activity or universal protection.
verification_scope: Complete primary Results/Discussion/Experimental Procedures inspected. No raw fluorescence, chromatogram or microscopy reanalysis.

starting_question: Do multiple associations indicate one proteolytic role, direct hydrolase activity, or scaffolding of distinct partners?
actual_observations: Authors: purified NlpI binds several endopeptidases; pairwise interactions alone do not establish simultaneous binding.
Authors: preformed partner complexes and controls support ternary assemblies; activity changes vary by hydrolase.
Authors: PBP1A does not bind NlpI directly in the tested assay but can associate through PBP4.
annotation_consequence: In-vitro scaffolding capacity is supported; the proposed physiological organization and coordination of synthesis remain incompletely demonstrated.
